title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 11 (Power to Take Samples)

content.overview: Section 11 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers any person authorised by the Central Government to take samples of air, water, soil or other substance from any factory, premises or place for analysis. The section prescribes procedural safeguards including notice to the occupier, division of samples and sealing, so that results can support enforcement and prosecution under the Act.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Authorised sampler? (2) Notice to occupier? (3) Sample divided and sealed as required? (4) Analysis path intact?
content.study:
Sampling procedure is critical for evidentiary use in penalty or direction proceedings. Defects in notice, division or sealing can weaken the sample's reliability.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Power to sample
sections.body: Authorised person may take samples of air, water, soil or other substance from any factory, premises or other place for the purpose of analysis.

sections.heading: Procedural safeguards
sections.body: Statutory requirements typically include notice to the occupier or agent, division of the sample into parts, and sealing/marking as the section provides — verify current text.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Samples support analysis for compliance assessment, directions under s. 5 and prosecution under s. 15.

sections.heading: Link to s. 10
sections.body: Entry under s. 10 often precedes sampling under s. 11; both require proper empowerment.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Prove authorisation, notice, division/sealing and chain to analysis.

provisions.title: Power to take sample and procedure to be followed

examples.title: Effluent sample
examples.body: Authorised officer takes an effluent sample after notice, divides and seals parts as s. 11 requires — analysis may support s. 15 prosecution or s. 5 directions.

hypotheticals.question: Is a sample taken without notice always inadmissible?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 11 procedural requirements exist to protect reliability and fairness; consequences of non-compliance depend on the statutory text and the forum's approach to statutory procedure.

distinctions.title: s. 11 samples vs s. 10 entry
distinctions.left: Taking and processing samples for analysis with procedural safeguards.

misconceptions.trap: Any grab sample without procedure can sustain EPA penalty.
misconceptions.correction: s. 11 lays down sampling procedure; compliance with that procedure is material to reliable use of the sample.
